teaser.text: Accenture is a large business-services company that helps organizations change how they work. Its customers pay for specialist people, technology and know-how, while Accenture pays the people and suppliers who deliver the result.

dividend.title: Accenture dividend
dividend.meta_description: Accenture dividend history, cash coverage, forecast changes and current yield against the share price.
dividend.opening: Accenture's dividend is $6.84 a year at the declared $1.71 quarterly rate. FY2026 real free cash flow after stock-based pay was $9.52 billion, compared with $3.987 billion of dividends paid.
dividend.closing: The full memo also explains Accenture's business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does Accenture pay in dividends?

paragraphs.text: The dividend begins at $6.84, annualized from the declared $1.71 quarterly rate. The base case then grows it near 8% annually, supported by guided free cash flow of $11.0–$11.8 billion and $9.5 billion of capital return. The bear case uses roughly 3% growth after FY2027; the bull uses roughly 11%, requiring stronger recurring AI and cybersecurity work. FY2026 dividends of $3.987 billion provide a cash-return anchor.

blocks.heading: Is Accenture's dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: Dividends rose from US$2,457,306 thousand in fiscal 2022 to US$3,987,313 thousand in fiscal 2026. In fiscal 2025, dividends and buybacks represented 85.9% of real free cash flow; in fiscal 2024, they exceeded that year’s generation. Accenture also sold US$1,341,025 thousand of new shares in fiscal 2026. Debt later became more important, with $5 billion of senior unsecured notes outstanding by August 2025.

Stock compensation was $2.1 billion. It is recorded as an expense but added back to operating cash because granting shares does not immediately use cash. Economically, however, the payment still transfers value from existing owners through dilution or through cash repurchases. Deducting it leaves a stricter free-cash-flow measure of $9.52 billion.

paragraphs.text: During FY2027–FY2029, AI projects must move into production and generate repeat work at healthy prices rather than reduce paid hours and fees. In FY2027, the planned $8 billion of acquisition investment must produce follow-on work and cash returns while Accenture funds dividends and buybacks. FY2027 federal demand is expected to improve after reducing FY2026 growth; the test is whether this is a lasting recovery or mainly an easier comparison. The federal investigation and unresolved U.S.–Ireland tax agreement remain risks to earnings and cash following FY2026.

blocks.heading: What is Accenture's dividend yield today?

paragraphs.text: Cash matters too. A 9.4% free-cash-flow yield and a 3.3% dividend yield provide useful starting measures, but acquisitions also consume cash. Buybacks can lift earnings per share without improving the business: Accenture expects its share count to fall about 3% in FY27, which could raise EPS about 3.1% if total profit stays unchanged.

earnings.opening: Accenture's next results are expected on December 17, 2026. The key thing to watch is whether AI and acquisitions become recurring, profitable work while federal and tax risks remain contained.
earnings.closing: The full memo covers Accenture's business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: What has Accenture guided for FY27?

paragraphs.text: Accenture helps clients change how they operate by designing, installing or running technology. It measures underlying growth in local currency so exchange rates do not disguise what clients actually bought: if a European client pays the same €1 million while the euro rises, dollar revenue increases even though the business did not. Management expects FY27 local-currency revenue growth of 3.0%–6.0%, with no material currency effect.

The same distinction affects earnings per share. Management guides to $14.39–$14.81, but FY27 growth is 6.0%–9.0% against reported earnings and only 3.0%–6.0% against adjusted earnings. Accenture also expects its share count to fall about 3%, so buybacks can lift EPS even if total profit grows more slowly. Acquisitions are expected to add 2.0%–2.5% to growth, leaving an indicative underlying contribution of roughly 0.5–4 percentage points.

blocks.heading: Did Accenture keep its past promises?

paragraphs.text: Management’s fiscal 2026 results met or exceeded its original promises on revenue growth, adjusted earnings and shareholder returns. Diluted shares also fell, showing that repurchases did more than absorb new equity.

blocks.heading: What has Accenture's revenue and profit done over the last eight quarters?

paragraphs.text: Profit requires adjustment. Reported EPS rose 46.2%, but the comparable increase was about 8.6% because the August 2025 quarter contained the full restructuring charge. Operating margin improved only modestly on that adjusted basis.

blocks.heading: What should you watch in Accenture's next results?

paragraphs.text: The decisive test is whether AI and acquisitions become recurring, profitable work while federal and tax risks remain contained.
